Regarding the definition of "zero-shot generalization" in the context of text-to-image AIs, it seems sensible. The concept of zero-shot generalization refers to the ability of a model to apply its learned knowledge to new, unseen concepts without requiring additional training data. In the context of text-to-image AIs, this means that the model can generate images based on text prompts without having seen the specific images or concepts before.

The 2013 paper cited in the response likely discussed the challenges and limitations of achieving zero-shot generalization in text-to-image AIs, and how it relates to the model's ability to learn and generalize from limited training data. The definition of zero-shot generalization in this context highlights the potential for text-to-image AIs to be more versatile and adaptable, and to generate a wider range of images based on text prompts.

It's worth noting that achieving zero-shot generalization in text-to-image AIs is still an active area of research, and there are many challenges to overcome, such as dealing with ambiguity, handling out-of-distribution inputs, and ensuring that the generated images are coherent and meaningful. However, the concept of zero-shot generalization provides a useful framework for understanding the potential capabilities and limitations of text-to-image AIs.
